Immunoglobulin M (Ig M) titers were normal [5]. The CD4 cell count of the patient was within the normal range, measuring 950 cells/mm3.

report.source_text: Initially, the treatment regimen included an oral tablet of prednisolone 60 mg/day and a tablet of Septran DS twice daily. Still, the patient did not show any improvement so he was started on valganciclovir - an oral loading dose of Valganciclovir 900 mg once daily dose for 21 days followed by a maintenance dose of 450 mg once daily for 6 weeks and oral prednisolone, which was tapered over 6 weeks.

clinician.final_diagnosis: cytomegalovirus retinitis with a macular star in an immunocompetent individual
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 40-year-old man presented with diminished vision in the right eye persisting for five months after trauma causing traumatic cataract and hand movement vision. Initial postoperative fundus examination of the right eye was normal. Laboratory tests showed normal immune status with elevated CMV IgG titers and normal CMV IgM and CD4 counts, supporting prior CMV exposure but no immunosuppression. Initial treatment with oral prednisolone and Septran was ineffective. Subsequently, valganciclovir therapy was initiated. After 1.5 months of valganciclovir, visual acuity improved to 6/6 and fundus examination revealed a healing choroiditis patch with resolving hemorrhagic patch and a macular star, confirming cytomegalovirus retinitis with macular star in an immunocompetent patient.
